about: The interior of a kidney, drawn once and used for both sides: capsule, cortex, medullary pyramids and renal columns, calyces and pelvis, the renal artery and vein with their branches, a scatter of glomeruli, and one nephron enlarged so that its course from glomerulus to collecting duct can be followed. Activity is the simulator's own filtration, flow and hormone signals pushing on each structure, shown as glow. The layout is schematic: nine pyramids, no arcuate or cortical radiate vessels, one nephron standing for about a million, and no dimension is a measurement. Finer structures (marked as children in the Structures list) appear when their parent is selected or the camera is close; they are schematic drawings, and counts, sizes and layout are illustrative, not measured.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Renal Capsule
parts.summary: The tough fibrous skin that wraps the whole kidney
parts.function: The capsule is a thin fibrous layer that surrounds the kidney and gives it its smooth outline. It is open only at the hilum, where the vessels and the pelvis pass through. It is drawn as glass so that the structures inside can be seen through it.

parts.label: Renal Cortex
parts.summary: The outer layer, where blood is filtered in the glomeruli
parts.function: The cortex holds the glomeruli and the convoluted tubules, and it is where most of the filtering and reabsorbing is done. It also extends inward between the pyramids as the renal columns. It brightens when the simulated filtration rate rises and dims when it falls.

drives.note: A higher glomerular filtration rate means the cortical filters are working harder.
When filtration falls the cortical filters are passing less fluid.

parts.label: Medullary Pyramids
parts.summary: Cone-shaped tissue whose tips, the papillae, point at the calyces
parts.function: The pyramids contain the loops of Henle and the collecting ducts. The tissue around the loops is made very salty, and antidiuretic hormone lets the collecting ducts use that saltiness to pull water back and make concentrated urine. It brightens when the simulation's vasopressin activity rises or the body is dehydrated.

drives.note: Vasopressin makes the collecting ducts permeable to water so the medulla can concentrate the urine.
A raised plasma osmolality raises vasopressin and so the concentrating work of the medulla.

parts.label: Renal Columns
parts.summary: Cortex that dips down between the pyramids
parts.function: The columns are cortical tissue that reaches inward between neighbouring pyramids. They support the pyramids and carry the interlobar vessels toward the cortex.

parts.label: Renal Pelvis and Calyces
parts.summary: The funnel that gathers urine from the papillae into the ureter
parts.function: A small cup, the minor calyx, wraps each papilla; the minor calyces join into three major calyces, and these open into the renal pelvis, which narrows into the ureter. Urine drips from the papillae into the cups and is carried down by gentle contractions of the walls. It brightens as urine flow rises.

drives.note: The more urine the papillae deliver, the more the calyces and pelvis have to carry.

parts.label: Renal Artery and Branches
parts.summary: Brings blood to the kidney; divides into segmental and interlobar arteries
parts.function: The renal artery enters the hilum and divides into segmental arteries, which give interlobar arteries that run in the columns between the pyramids. The juxtaglomerular cells that release renin sit on the smallest branches that feed the glomeruli. It brightens when cardiac output rises or renin release is driven, and dims when blood pressure falls.

drives.note: More cardiac output sends more blood down the renal artery.
A low arterial pressure reduces the flow the artery carries.
Renin is released by the juxtaglomerular cells on the finest arterial branches.

parts.label: Renal Vein
parts.summary: Carries filtered blood out of the kidney
parts.function: Blood that has passed through the glomerular and tubular capillaries drains through the interlobar veins into the renal vein, which leaves the hilum in front of the artery. It is drawn in the colour of venous blood, though kidney blood stays fairly oxygenated because the kidney receives far more blood than its own tissue needs.

parts.label: Glomeruli
parts.summary: Tufts of capillaries in the cortex where blood is filtered
parts.function: Each glomerulus is a ball of capillaries inside a cup, Bowman's capsule, and fluid is pushed through its wall under blood pressure to form the filtrate. The simulation's glomerular filtration rate is the sum of this filtering. They glow more when filtration is above rest and less when it falls.

drives.note: Filtration is the glomeruli's work, so a higher rate means brighter glomeruli.
When filtration collapses the glomeruli are passing little fluid.

parts.label: Nephron (enlarged)
parts.summary: One nephron drawn large: capsule, tubule, loop of Henle, collecting duct
parts.function: The filtrate leaves Bowman's capsule and passes through the proximal convoluted tubule, down and up the loop of Henle, through the distal convoluted tubule and into a collecting duct that runs down a pyramid to the papilla. Along the way water and salts are reclaimed and the urine is made; aldosterone acts on the later segments to retain sodium. The pale stream in it thins when filtration falls.

drives.note: More filtrate means more fluid passing through every nephron.
Less filtrate means less fluid in the tubule.
Aldosterone acts on the distal nephron and collecting duct to retain sodium.

parts.label: Hilum
parts.summary: The notch on the inner edge where vessels and the pelvis enter and leave
parts.function: The hilum is the doorway on the medial side of the kidney. The renal artery and vein, nerves, lymphatics and the renal pelvis all pass through it into the renal sinus. It is drawn as a ring where the cortex stops.

parts.label: Renal Sinus
parts.summary: The fat-filled space inside the kidney that holds the pelvis and vessels
parts.function: The sinus is the cavity that opens at the hilum and lies inside the kidney. It holds the calyces, the pelvis, the main branches of the renal vessels and a packing of fat. It is drawn as a pale glass envelope round that space.

parts.label: Perirenal Fat
parts.summary: A cushion of fat round the kidney, outside its capsule
parts.function: The perirenal fat lies between the capsule and the renal fascia and surrounds the kidney and the adrenal gland. It cushions the kidney and holds it in place. It is drawn as a loose glass shell with a gap at the hilum.

parts.label: Renal Fascia
parts.summary: The membrane that encloses the kidney and its fat
parts.function: The renal fascia is a sheet of connective tissue that wraps the kidney, the adrenal gland and the perirenal fat. It anchors the kidney to the abdominal wall. It is drawn as a thin glass shell outside the fat.

parts.label: Minor Calyces
parts.summary: Cups that catch urine from the tip of each pyramid
parts.function: Each minor calyx cups the papilla of one pyramid and collects the urine that drips from it. Several minor calyces join to form a major calyx. In this drawing the cups lie inside the pelvis drawing and show in a stronger colour.

drives.note: More urine leaving the papillae means more passing through the calyces.

parts.label: Major Calyces
parts.summary: Wider channels that gather the minor calyces into the pelvis
parts.function: The major calyces are the next channel in the urine pathway. Each receives several minor calyces and empties into the renal pelvis. They are drawn as the three branches that meet at the pelvis.

drives.note: The calyces carry all of the urine the kidney makes.

parts.label: Renal Papillae
parts.summary: The rounded tips of the pyramids that point into the calyces
parts.function: A papilla is the apex of a medullary pyramid. The collecting ducts open on its surface, and urine leaves the kidney tissue here for the minor calyx. One cone is drawn on each pyramid.

drives.note: Urine drips from the collecting ducts at the papillary tips.
Vasopressin sets how concentrated the urine is by the time it reaches the tip.

parts.label: Interlobar Arteries
parts.summary: Arteries that run between the pyramids toward the cortex
parts.function: The interlobar arteries are branches of the segmental arteries. They climb through the renal columns between the pyramids and, at the base of each pyramid, turn into the arcuate arteries.

drives.note: A higher cardiac output sends more blood through the renal arteries.

parts.label: Interlobar Veins
parts.summary: Veins that run beside the interlobar arteries
parts.function: The interlobar veins drain the arcuate veins and travel back toward the sinus alongside the arteries. They join to form the renal vein.

parts.label: Arcuate Arteries
parts.summary: Arteries that arch over the base of each pyramid
parts.function: The arcuate arteries bend along the boundary between cortex and medulla, over the base of a pyramid. They give off the interlobular arteries that climb into the cortex.

parts.label: Arcuate Veins
parts.summary: Veins that arch over the base of each pyramid
parts.function: The arcuate veins run along the corticomedullary boundary beside the arteries and collect blood from the interlobular veins. They empty into the interlobar veins.

parts.label: Interlobular Arteries
parts.summary: Fine arteries that rise through the cortex
parts.function: The interlobular arteries (also called cortical radiate arteries) rise from the arcuate arteries through the cortex. They give off the afferent arterioles that feed the glomeruli.

parts.label: Interlobular Veins
parts.summary: Fine veins that descend through the cortex
parts.function: The interlobular veins collect blood from the capillaries around the tubules in the cortex and carry it down to the arcuate veins.

parts.label: Juxtaglomerular Apparatus
parts.summary: The meeting point of a tubule and its own glomerulus, where renin is made
parts.function: At the entry to the glomerulus the distal tubule touches the afferent and efferent arterioles. The cells here sense salt delivery and blood pressure and release renin, which starts a chain of hormones that raises blood pressure. It is drawn enlarged beside the enlarged nephron.

drives.note: Renin release rises with sympathetic drive and a fall in perfusion.
A fall in arterial pressure lowers stretch in the afferent arteriole and raises renin release.

parts.label: Afferent Arteriole
parts.summary: The small vessel that brings blood into the glomerulus
parts.function: The afferent arteriole delivers blood from the interlobular artery to the tuft of capillaries. Its muscle narrows or widens to control how much blood is filtered.

parts.label: Efferent Arteriole
parts.summary: The small vessel that carries blood out of the glomerulus
parts.function: The efferent arteriole drains the tuft and leads on to the capillaries around the tubules. Narrowing it raises the pressure inside the glomerulus.

parts.label: Glomerular Capillaries
parts.summary: The tuft of fenestrated capillaries where blood is filtered
parts.function: The glomerular capillaries are a coiled tuft of very leaky capillaries. Water and small solutes cross their wall into the capsule, while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

drives.note: A higher filtration rate means more fluid crossing the capillary wall.
A lower filtration rate means less fluid crossing.

parts.label: Bowman's Capsule
parts.summary: The cup that surrounds the glomerulus and catches the filtrate
parts.function: Bowman's capsule is the blind, expanded start of the nephron. It wraps the capillary tuft and passes the filtrate on into the proximal tubule. It has an outer parietal layer and an inner visceral layer.

parts.label: Parietal Layer
parts.summary: The flat outer wall of the capsule
parts.function: The parietal layer is a single sheet of flat cells that forms the outer wall of Bowman's capsule. At the urinary pole it becomes the lining of the proximal tubule.

parts.label: Visceral Layer
parts.summary: The inner layer of the capsule, made of podocytes, that covers the capillaries
parts.function: The visceral layer clings to the capillary tuft. Its cells are the podocytes, whose fine processes form the last barrier the filtrate crosses.

parts.label: Podocytes
parts.summary: Octopus-like cells that wrap the glomerular capillaries
parts.function: Podocytes are the cells of the visceral layer. Their foot processes interlock around the capillaries and leave narrow slits that let the filtrate through while holding back large proteins.

parts.label: Mesangial Cells
parts.summary: Supporting cells between the capillary loops
parts.function: Mesangial cells lie among the capillary loops of the glomerulus and hold the tuft together. They can contract and so change the surface available for filtration, and they clear debris from the filter.

parts.label: Proximal Convoluted Tubule
parts.summary: The first coiled stretch, which takes back most of the filtrate
parts.function: The proximal tubule has a brush border and many mitochondria. It reabsorbs most of the filtered water, salt, glucose and amino acids and returns them to the blood.

drives.note: More filtrate arriving means more to reabsorb.
Less filtrate arriving means less to reabsorb.

parts.label: Descending Limb
parts.summary: The thin straight tube that dips into the medulla
parts.function: The descending limb of the loop of Henle is thin-walled and permeable to water. As it passes down through salty tissue, water leaves it and the fluid inside becomes more concentrated.

drives.note: The concentrating work of the medulla follows vasopressin.

parts.label: Thin Ascending Limb
parts.summary: The thin tube that climbs back after the hairpin bend
parts.function: The thin ascending limb is permeable to salt but not to water, so salt leaves it as the fluid climbs. It leads into the thick ascending limb.

parts.label: Thick Ascending Limb
parts.summary: The thick tube that pumps salt out and returns to the cortex
parts.function: The thick ascending limb actively moves salt out of the tubule but is tight to water. This builds the salty tissue of the medulla and dilutes the fluid in the tubule.

drives.note: Distal salt handling is tuned by aldosterone.

parts.label: Macula Densa
parts.summary: A patch of crowded cells that senses salt in the tubule
parts.function: The macula densa is a plaque of tightly packed cells where the thick ascending limb touches its own glomerulus. It senses how much salt is arriving and signals the arterioles and the renin cells.

drives.note: Low salt delivery to the macula densa raises renin release.

parts.label: Distal Convoluted Tubule
parts.summary: The second coiled stretch, where fine adjustment begins
parts.function: The distal tubule takes back more salt and, under the control of hormones, adjusts how much calcium and potassium is kept or lost.

drives.note: Aldosterone increases salt retention and potassium loss in the distal nephron.

parts.label: Connecting Tubule
parts.summary: The short link between the distal tubule and the collecting duct
parts.function: The connecting tubule joins the distal tubule to the collecting duct and shares features of both. Several nephrons empty into one collecting duct.

drives.note: Aldosterone acts on the cells of this segment.

parts.label: Collecting Duct
parts.summary: The straight duct that carries urine through the pyramid to the papilla
parts.function: The collecting duct passes down through the medulla. Where vasopressin is present its wall becomes permeable to water, which leaves into the salty tissue and makes the urine more concentrated.

drives.note: Vasopressin opens water channels in the duct wall.
Dehydration raises vasopressin.

parts.label: Principal Cells
parts.summary: The main cells of the collecting duct, which respond to vasopressin and aldosterone
parts.function: Principal cells take back salt and, when vasopressin is present, let water through. They are the larger, paler cells in the wall of the collecting duct.

drives.note: Vasopressin inserts water channels in these cells.
Aldosterone raises their salt uptake.

parts.label: Intercalated Cells
parts.summary: The dark cells that adjust the acid and bicarbonate in the urine
parts.function: Intercalated cells are scattered among the principal cells. They secrete acid or bicarbonate and so help to keep the blood's acidity steady.

parts.label: Peritubular Capillaries
parts.summary: The capillary network that surrounds the tubules in the cortex
parts.function: The peritubular capillaries continue from the efferent arteriole and twine round the convoluted tubules. They take back the water and solutes the tubules reabsorb.

parts.label: Vasa Recta
parts.summary: Hairpin capillaries that run beside the loops of Henle
parts.function: The vasa recta are long, thin capillary loops that follow the loops of Henle into the medulla. Their hairpin shape lets them supply the medulla without washing away its salty gradient.

parts.label: Granular (Juxtaglomerular) Cells
parts.summary: Modified muscle cells in the afferent arteriole that store and release renin
parts.function: The granular cells are specialised smooth-muscle cells in the wall of the afferent arteriole. They hold renin in granules and release it when pressure or salt delivery falls or when sympathetic nerves are active.

drives.note: Sympathetic drive and low perfusion release renin from these cells.

parts.label: Macula Densa Contact
parts.summary: Where the distal tubule's sensing patch meets the glomerulus
parts.function: This is the point of contact between the macula densa and the arterioles at the entry to the glomerulus. The signal passes across it from tubule to vessel. In this drawing a thin bridge joins the two, because the enlarged nephron cannot be drawn doubling back on itself.

parts.label: Extraglomerular Mesangium
parts.summary: The cluster of cells in the angle between the arterioles and the macula densa
parts.function: The extraglomerular mesangium (also called the lacis cells) fills the space between the two arterioles and the macula densa. It is continuous with the mesangium inside the glomerulus and passes signals between the sensing and renin-making cells.
